summary: Streamed queries persist NULL input_tokens/output_tokens — missing stream_options.include_usage
description:
Streamed responses to /api/query persist with input_tokens/output_tokens = NULL because OpenAI-compatible streaming omits usage by default. Three independent gaps, all verified against current code.

Gap 1 — src/lib/model.ts:63-74 (completeStream)
Missing stream_options: { include_usage: true } on the chat.completions.create call. Without it, the API never emits a usage chunk. Non-streaming complete() at line 46 doesn't need this — non-streamed responses always include usage.

Gap 2 — src/app/api/query/route.ts:69-75
The for-await loop only reads chunk.choices[0]?.delta?.content. Even if a usage chunk arrived, nothing extracts chunk.usage. The usage chunk's choices[] is empty, so the existing content path naturally skips it.

Gap 3 — src/app/api/query/route.ts:97-111
INSERT INTO queries lists 7 columns; input_tokens / output_tokens are absent. Schema (migrations/002_sessions_queries.sql:22-23) already has them as nullable INTEGER, so no migration needed.

Field-name bridge: API returns prompt_tokens / completion_tokens; DB columns are input_tokens / output_tokens. Map at the INSERT site.

Edge cases:
- Stream truncation: declare counters as `let inputTokens: number | null = null` alongside fullResponse. Only assign inside the loop when chunk.usage is present. NULL on truncation is distinguishable from a legitimate 0-token response.
- chunk.usage is typed as possibly undefined on ChatCompletionChunk — a plain `if (chunk.usage)` guard is enough, no type assertion.
- max_tokens is independent of include_usage.

OpenRouter caveat: include_usage is generally honored and forwarded for both configured models (deepseek/deepseek-chat, anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5), but worth a one-off verification per model since OpenRouter normalizes Anthropic's native usage shape and normalization bugs occasionally surface.

Fix size: ~3 small edits, no migration. Root cause understood — go straight to todo-implement when picking this up.
